chunks: Abu Ali Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abduwayh narrated to us. He said: Abu Abdillah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Rijal al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Hakam narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, from Mutrif, from al-Sha'bi, from his uncle Qays ibn Abd, who said:

We were sitting in a circle in which was Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, when a Bedouin came and said: "Which one of you is Abdullah?" Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "I am Abdullah." He said: "Has your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ever told you how many caliphs would come after him?" He said: "Yes, twelve, like the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel."

key_terms.الخلفاء: Caliphs/successors — those who succeed the Prophet in leadership
key_terms.بني إسرائيل: Children of Israel — descendants of Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob)
key_terms.نقباء: Chiefs/leaders — twelve tribal chiefs among the Children of Israel

ai.seo_question: How many caliphs did the Prophet Muhammad say would come after him?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through a chain going back to the prominent companion Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, records a Bedouin's inquiry about the number of caliphs after the Prophet Muhammad (s). Ibn Mas'ud confirms that the Prophet stated there would be twelve successors, equal to the number of chiefs (nuqaba') appointed among the Children of Israel, as referenced in the Quran (5:12). This narration is a key text in Twelver Shia theology.
